meta.title: Standard Solution Preparation and Standardization Procedure

sections.purpose: To establish a uniform procedure for preparation, standardization, and management of volumetric standard solutions used in titrimetric analysis in pharmaceutical laboratories, ensuring accuracy and traceability as per IP/BP/USP requirements.
sections.scope: Applicable to all pharmacy laboratory departments for preparation of primary and secondary standard solutions including N/10 HCl, N/10 NaOH, N/10 H₂SO₄, 0.1 M sodium thiosulphate, and all other volumetric solutions used in official pharmacopeial methods.
procedure: Identify the standard solution required and consult the approved IP/BP/USP method for the exact preparation protocol.

Classify the standard as: Primary standard — prepared from a reference-grade chemical of known high purity (e.g., anhydrous sodium carbonate, potassium hydrogen phthalate, potassium dichromate); Secondary standard — prepared approximately and standardized against a primary standard.

For primary standard solutions: dry the primary standard chemical at the specified temperature (e.g., anhydrous Na₂CO₃ at 270°C for 1 hour); allow to cool in a desiccator; weigh the exact amount on an analytical balance (4 decimal places).
Dissolve the primary standard in freshly boiled and cooled distilled water in a volumetric flask; make up to the exact volume.
For secondary standard solutions (e.g., NaOH, HCl): prepare the solution of approximately the required normality by dissolving or diluting the chemical; transfer to a graduated storage bottle.
Standardize the secondary solution: titrate 3 separate aliquots of the prepared solution against the appropriate primary standard; calculate the exact normality/molarity from each titration.
Calculate the factor F: Actual normality = Weighed amount / (Equivalent weight × Volume); Factor F = Actual normality / Theoretical normality.
Accept if the factor F is within 0.98–1.02 (i.e., the solution concentration is within 2% of the nominal value) — if not, adjust the solution and re-standardize.
Label the standardized solution bottle: Solution name, Nominal concentration, Actual concentration/Factor F, Standardization date, Expiry date (typically 1 month), Standardized by, and Batch number.
Verify the standardization by a second analyst performing an independent titration — both analysts' results must agree within 0.2% relative.

Record all standardization details in the Standard Solution Register: chemical name and lot, preparation details, all individual titration volumes, calculated factor, second analyst verification, and approver's signature.
Re-standardize the solution at the specified frequency (monthly or as per the pharmacopoeia) and whenever there is doubt about the solution's integrity.
Discard expired or failed standardizations and prepare fresh solution.
precautions: Use only pharmacopeial-grade or certified reference standard chemicals for primary standards — never use ordinary laboratory reagent grade chemicals.
Dry primary standards at the exact temperature and duration specified — incomplete drying or over-drying introduces systematic weighing errors.
Use Class A volumetric glassware for all standard solution preparations — Class B glassware has unacceptable tolerance for standard solutions.
Use freshly boiled and cooled distilled water for all aqueous standard solutions — dissolved CO₂ reacts with NaOH, altering its normality.
Store NaOH standard solution in plastic (polyethylene) bottles — glass leaches silicates that precipitate and alter normality.
Never use a standard solution beyond its expiry date — even if clarified and apparently unchanged, degradation may have occurred.
All standard solution preparations must be witnessed and countersigned by a second qualified person — GLP requirement.
